mergedParams.userDescription: Glitch text transition effect between two scenes.

prompts.prompt: Create a digital glitch text transition that corrupts the outgoing scene's text into fragmented pieces before reassembling into the incoming scene's text. Think of this like a video editor would approach a glitch transition - the text should appear to break apart into RGB color channels that separate and distort with digital artifacts (horizontal displacement, random character substitution, flickering opacity). The transition should have three phases: corruption (300ms), peak glitch (200ms), and reconstruction (300ms). Use a staggered approach where different parts of the text glitch at slightly different times to create an organic, chaotic feel. The glitch should feel violent and jarring, like a broken VHS tape or corrupted digital signal.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: Two BaseLayout containers (one for each scene) with absolute positioning using 'absolute inset-0'. Each scene contains a TextAtom wrapped in a BaseLayout. Apply a custom glitch effect using generic keyframe animations on multiple properties simultaneously: translateX (random -20px to 20px jitter), opacity (flicker between 0.3-1), and custom CSS filters for RGB channel separation using 'drop-shadow' filters. Use three duplicate text layers per scene with 'absolute inset-0' positioning, each with different blend modes ('screen', 'multiply', 'overlay') and slight translateX offsets (-2px, 0, 2px) to simulate RGB separation. Implement character substitution by rapidly switching between the original text and glitched characters using visibility toggling at 60fps intervals. Use 'will-change-transform' for GPU acceleration. Timing: Scene 1 visible 0-0.8, Scene 2 visible 0.8-end. Apply easing: 'steps(4)' for digital stuttering effect. Consider using internal effect presets for the glitch artifacts that can be reused across multiple text elements.

prompts.prompt: Design a smooth, cinematic text crossfade transition with motion blur simulation between scenes. Imagine this as a professional video dissolve where the outgoing text gradually loses focus and fades out while simultaneously, the incoming text fades in from a blurred state to sharp focus. The transition should feel like a camera pulling focus between two depth planes. Add subtle horizontal movement - the outgoing text drifts slightly left while fading out, and the incoming text drifts in from slightly right. This creates a parallax effect that adds depth to the transition. The overall timing should be elegant and measured, taking 1.2 seconds total with overlapping fade periods.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use two BaseLayout containers with 'relative w-full h-full' positioning. Each contains a TextAtom centered with 'flex items-center justify-center'. Implement motion blur using CSS filter blur() starting at 0px, ramping to 8px, then back to 0px for the incoming text. Combine with opacity animations (1 to 0 for outgoing, 0 to 1 for incoming) over overlapping ranges. Add translateX animations: outgoing moves from 0 to -30px, incoming from 30px to 0. Use 'ease-in-out' easing for smooth acceleration/deceleration. Apply 'transform-gpu' class for hardware acceleration. Consider using generic keyframe effects with AnimationRange arrays for precise control. Timing strategy: Scene 1 effects from 0-0.7, Scene 2 effects from 0.5-1.2 (0.2 second overlap). Use fitDurationTo: 'children' to ensure proper timing inheritance.

prompts.prompt: Build a typewriter-style character reveal transition where the outgoing text deletes character by character from right to left, followed by the incoming text typing in character by character from left to right. Include a blinking cursor element that persists throughout the transition. Add mechanical typing sounds synced to each character appearance/disappearance. The deletion should feel slightly faster than the typing (like holding backspace), while the typing should have irregular rhythm to feel human. Include subtle screen shake on each keystroke for tactile feedback.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with a parent BaseLayout using 'flex items-center justify-center min-h-screen'. Use caption data with word-level timing to control character reveals. For the typewriter effect, wrap each character in a span with individual opacity control. Implement using TextAtom with custom rendering that splits text into characters. Create a cursor using ShapeAtom with 'w-0.5 h-6 bg-white' classes, animated with opacity 0-1 at 500ms intervals. Apply micro-shake effect using translateX/Y with random values between -1px and 1px on each character reveal. Use internal effect presets for the shake that triggers on each character. Timing: Deletion at 30ms per character, typing at 50-80ms per character (randomized). Include AudioAtom for typewriter sounds, triggered using time ranges synchronized with character timings. Consider using sub-presets: one for the typewriter effect, one for the cursor, composed together.

prompts.prompt: Create a matrix-style digital rain transition where the outgoing text dissolves into falling green characters that cascade down the screen, eventually forming the incoming text. The characters should fall at different speeds with trailing fade effects, creating depth. Some characters should randomly change as they fall (like the Matrix digital rain). The incoming text should materialize from these falling characters, first as random characters that quickly resolve into the correct letters. Add a subtle green glow and scanline effect for authenticity.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use a full-screen BaseLayout with 'absolute inset-0 bg-black overflow-hidden'. Create multiple columns (20-30) using CSS Grid ('grid grid-cols-20 gap-1'). Each column contains vertically stacked characters using BaseLayout with 'flex flex-col'. Implement falling animation using translateY from -100% to 200% with varying animation durations (2-5s) per column. Apply staggered delays using repeatChildrenProps with incremental timing offsets. Characters use TextAtom with 'text-green-400 font-mono text-sm' classes. Add glow using 'drop-shadow(0 0 10px rgb(74 222 128))' filter. Create trailing effect with opacity gradient: characters at top have opacity 0.2, increasing to 1 at the falling edge. For text materialization, use generic keyframe effects to transition from random characters to final text over 500ms. Add scanline effect using a semi-transparent BaseLayout with 'bg-gradient-to-b from-transparent via-green-400/10 to-transparent' animated with translateY. Consider using waveform effects if audio is present to make rain react to sound.

prompts.prompt: Develop a shattered glass transition where the outgoing text appears to break into sharp, angular fragments that explode outward, revealing the incoming text beneath. Each fragment should have realistic physics - larger pieces fall faster, smaller pieces float longer. Add depth with shadows and 3D rotation on fragments. The shatter should originate from a specific impact point (center of text) with radial explosion. Include a brief 'crack' formation before the full shatter, and subtle particle effects for glass dust.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure using two BaseLayout layers with 'absolute inset-0'. Outgoing text uses clip-path polygons to create 8-12 irregular fragments. Generate fragments using BaseLayout with 'absolute' positioning, each containing a TextAtom with the full text but different clip-path values to show only portions. Implement explosion using transform: translate3d() with radial vectors from center point, combined with rotateX/Y/Z for tumbling effect. Large fragments: translateY increases faster (gravity simulation), small fragments: add translateX wobble. Use 'preserve-3d' transform-style for 3D effect. Add shadows using 'drop-shadow(2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.3))'. Crack formation: 200ms with SVG crack overlay, then explosion over 800ms. Particle effects: 20+ small ShapeAtom elements with 'w-1 h-1 bg-white opacity-60' animated with random trajectories. Timing: crack at 0-0.2, shatter 0.2-1.0, incoming text fades in 0.5-1.0. Use 'ease-out' for explosion, 'ease-in' for gravity.

prompts.prompt: Design a liquid morph transition where text appears to melt and flow like liquid metal between the two scenes. The outgoing text should liquify from bottom to top, pooling at the bottom of the screen, then reform from this pool into the incoming text, rising from bottom to top. Add realistic liquid physics with wobbling, surface tension effects, and metallic reflections. Include dripping effects for individual letters and viscous movement timing.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use SVG filters for liquid distortion: turbulence and displacement filters applied to TextAtom elements. Structure with BaseLayout containing both text layers. Apply CSS transforms: scaleY animation from 1 to 0.1 (melting) and 0.1 to 1 (reforming), combined with translateY to simulate pooling. Add skewX oscillation (-5deg to 5deg) for wobble effect. Implement drips using pseudo-elements or additional ShapeAtom components with 'bg-gradient-to-b from-current to-transparent' positioned absolutely below letters. Use cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) for viscous movement. Add metallic effect with gradient background: 'bg-gradient-to-b from-gray-300 via-gray-100 to-gray-300' and mix-blend-mode: 'overlay'. Apply turbulence filter with baseFrequency animating from 0 to 0.02 for ripple effect. Timing: melt 0-0.6, pool state 0.6-0.7, reform 0.7-1.3. Consider using internal effect presets for the wobble and drip animations.

prompts.prompt: Create a glitch-art datamosh transition that simulates video compression artifacts between scenes. The outgoing text should appear to 'smear' horizontally as if key frames are missing, creating motion trails and pixel bleeding effects. Add compression blocks, color channel shifts, and macro-blocking artifacts. The incoming text emerges from this digital chaos as the compression 'catches up' and the image stabilizes. Include data corruption visual elements like hex code overlays and binary streams.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Layer structure: Use 3 BaseLayout containers stacked with 'absolute inset-0'. Bottom layer: outgoing text with horizontal motion blur using 'filter: blur(20px 0)'. Middle layer: compression blocks using Grid layout 'grid grid-cols-8 grid-rows-6' with ShapeAtom blocks randomly colored and opacity animated. Top layer: incoming text with reducing blur. Implement pixel smear using multiple duplicates of TextAtom with increasing translateX values (0, 20px, 40px, etc.) and decreasing opacity (1, 0.7, 0.4, etc.). Add RGB shift using three text copies with 'mix-blend-mode: screen' and translateX offsets with red, green, blue color filters. Macro-blocks: 8x6 grid of divs with random background colors sampled from text, opacity pulsing 0.3-1. Include hex overlay using small TextAtom elements with random hex values, positioned absolutely, rapidly changing content. Use requestAnimationFrame for 60fps updates on glitch elements. Timing: smear effect 0-0.5, peak corruption 0.5-0.7, stabilization 0.7-1.0.

prompts.prompt: Build an elastic bounce transition where outgoing text compresses vertically like it's being squashed, then springs away with elastic physics, while incoming text bounces in from the opposite direction. Add squash and stretch deformation for cartoon-like appeal. The bounce should have multiple decreasing oscillations, like a rubber ball coming to rest. Include motion lines and impact effects at the compression points.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure with BaseLayout using 'flex items-center justify-center h-full'. Apply transform-origin: 'center bottom' for squash effect. Outgoing text: animate scaleY from 1 to 0.3 (squash) over 200ms with ease-in, then scaleY to 1.5 and translateY to -200% (stretch and exit) over 300ms. Incoming text: start at translateY: 200% and scaleY: 1.5, animate to translateY: 0 with bouncing (use spring easing or keyframes with values: 0%, -20%, 0%, -10%, 0%, -5%, 0%). Add scaleX inverse relationship: when scaleY is 0.3, scaleX is 1.3 (volume preservation). Motion lines: use multiple BaseLayout divs with 'h-0.5 bg-gradient-to-r from-transparent to-current' positioned behind text during movement. Impact effect: ShapeAtom circle that scales from 0 to 200% with opacity 1 to 0 at compression point. Use cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) for main bounce, then dampening oscillations. Consider using internal effect presets for the squash-and-stretch deformation.

prompts.prompt: Design a portal warp transition where outgoing text gets sucked into a swirling vortex at the center of the screen, disappearing into a singularity, then incoming text emerges from the same point with reverse vortex motion. Add gravitational distortion effects where text stretches as it approaches the center. Include particle effects being pulled into/expelled from the vortex, and a subtle space-time distortion grid in the background.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create vortex using CSS transforms on TextAtom: combine rotate (0 to 720deg), scale (1 to 0), and radial translation. Calculate spiral path using parametric equations: x = t * cos(t*4), y = t * sin(t*4) where t goes from 0 to 1. Implement using keyframes at 10% intervals for smooth spiral. Add perspective: 1000px to parent BaseLayout for 3D depth. Text distortion: use scaleX based on distance from center (farther = more stretched). Background grid: SVG pattern or CSS grid 'grid grid-cols-20 grid-rows-20' with lines that bend toward center using transform skew. Particle system: 30+ ShapeAtom dots with 'w-1 h-1 rounded-full bg-white' following similar spiral paths with varied timing. Singularity effect: ShapeAtom circle at center with radial gradient 'bg-gradient-radial from-purple-900 to-transparent' pulsing scale. Timing: suck-in 0-0.8, singularity pulse 0.8-0.9, emerge 0.9-1.7. Use ease-in for suck, ease-out for emerge. Consider audio analysis to sync vortex rotation speed with beat if audio present.

prompts.prompt: Create a newspaper print transition that simulates old printing press effects. Outgoing text fades while showing halftone dot patterns growing larger until text becomes unreadable, then incoming text prints in with registration marks, CMYK color separation layers building up, and ink bleeding effects. Add vintage newspaper texture, slight rotation misalignment between color plates, and a printing press roller animation that wipes across the screen.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Layer setup: 4 BaseLayout containers for CMYK separation, each with 'absolute inset-0 mix-blend-mode-multiply'. Outgoing text: apply SVG filter for halftone effect using feComponentTransfer and feConvolveMatrix, animate dot size from 1px to 20px. Color separation: duplicate TextAtom 4 times with cyan, magenta, yellow, black colors using 'text-cyan-500', 'text-pink-500', 'text-yellow-500', 'text-gray-900'. Each layer has slight offset: translateX/Y random -2px to 2px, rotate random -0.5deg to 0.5deg for misregistration. Roller animation: BaseLayout div with 'h-full w-12 bg-gradient-to-r from-gray-800 to-gray-600' moving translateX from -100% to 100% with linear timing. Ink bleed: CSS filter blur(0.5px) and increase to blur(2px) at edges. Newspaper texture: overlay BaseLayout with 'bg-noise opacity-10' (use CSS pattern or base64 SVG). Registration marks: ShapeAtom crosses positioned at corners with 'w-4 h-4' using intersecting rectangles. Timing: fade/halftone 0-0.6, roller wipe 0.6-1.0, CMYK build-up 0.7-1.2 with 100ms stagger between plates. Consider sub-preset for halftone effect generator.
